claims.text: Exactly what :func:`convene` would do, WITHOUT calling anything. No adapter method that could reach a vendor is touched: only the identity properties (actor, independence class, lane), which are pure.
claims.why: The claim depends on _round_body and _role_for not calling vendor methods; these are defined elsewhere in the file but not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: True only for a loopback HTTP endpoint. ``localhost``-ish and nothing else. "Local" was a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set; here it is a property of the RESOLVED host, checked, not asserted.
claims.why: The function checks if the host part of the URL is in _LOCAL_HOSTS (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost). It does not check environment variables.

claims.text: Lanes come from the council profiles, NOT from a default argument here: ``codex`` and ``agy`` are ``untrusted`` (allow-list tier ON) unless the operator opts in per council.
claims.why: The code does not show how lanes are assigned; it relies on CouncilAdapter initialization which is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY and ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is neither read for routing nor written -- normalising a remote Ollama into this process would retroactively falsify ``offload.py``'s ``lane="trusted"`` justification from a code path nobody edited.
claims.why: The code reads DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST from vendors module; whether that constant reads OLLAMA_HOST is not visible in this chunk.

observations.what: dry_run_plan returns a plan with 'advisory': True and estimated token counts based on _round_body and evidence text tokens. It does not call any vendor methods, but uses helper functions that may have side effects.
_is_local_http only matches HTTP URLs; other schemes (e.g., https) are not considered. The regex requires 'http' or 'https' at start.
default_participants imports adapters inside the function to avoid circular imports, but the docstring references offload.py which is not present in this chunk.
